c1.title: Your twin is a living curve
c1.body: It learns how your body handles food, sleep and walking, and draws where your sugar is heading next.

c2.title: It always says how sure it is
c2.body: The soft band around the curve is the twin's honesty. A wide band means it knows less right now.

c3.title: A finger-prick teaches it
c3.body: A new reading updates the twin. Usually the band narrows; if the reading surprises it, the band can widen, and the twin says so.

c4.title: Ask it anything, in your language
c4.body: Type a question in English, Spanish, French, German, Italian or Japanese. Numbers in the answer come from your twin's tools, and it never gives medicine doses.

trust.title: Trust panel
trust.subtitle: Every number here is read from the evaluation reports. Nothing is typed by hand.
trust.ladderCaption: Lower is better: the average forecast error (RMSE, mg/dL) at each look-ahead time.
trust.coverageCaption: Each bar shows how often the true value fell inside the band. The line marks the 90% target.
trust.calibrationCaption: If the twin says 30%, it should happen about 30% of the time. Dots near the diagonal are good.
trust.baselinesCaption: The same test, run with simpler forecasting methods.
trust.transferTitle: Does it work on a different population?
trust.transferCaption: Trained on one dataset, tested on another. The gap shows how well it travels.
trust.subgroupsCaption: Marked rows are groups where the twin is clearly less well calibrated.
trust.nbpCaption: The same number of readings a day, placed at different times. Lower error is better.
trust.errorGridCaption: Zone A is clinically accurate and B is harmless. Zones C to E could lead to a wrong action.
trust.calLengthTitle: How many days of CGM are needed?
trust.calLengthCaption: Accuracy after calibrating on different numbers of CGM days.
trust.limitationsTitle: What the twin cannot do yet
trust.sourcesFallback: Sources, citations and licences are listed in data/README.md in the repository.
trust.noIndianData: No open Indian CGM dataset is known. Indian meals are handled through an Indian food table, not by pretending the training data is Indian.
trust.reportsMissing: The evaluation reports have not been generated yet.
trust.headline: Headline
trust.mockNote: Offline mode: evaluation reports need the backend, so the model evaluation sections stay empty. The multilingual agent section shows an illustrative mock report, marked as not live; it is not an evaluation result.
trust.tileCoverage: How often the 90% band held the true value, 1 hour ahead, {{level}}
trust.tileAuroc: How well it ranks risky hours for going above 180 (AUROC, 1 = perfect, 0.5 = chance), {{level}}
trust.abstainNote: With {{level}}, the twin said “not sure” for {{rate}} of forecasts. Its 1-hour error was {{a}} mg/dL then, against {{b}} mg/dL when it was confident.
trust.widthNote: Under each bar: half-width of the band in mg/dL (the twin's ± range).
trust.eceNote: ECE is the average gap between the stated chance and what happened (0 = perfect). Calibration on held-out patients pulls the curve onto the diagonal.
trust.lowBody: Only {{pct}} of 2-hour windows contained a low ({{n}} windows in {{p}} patients). That is too few to train or check the chance of going low, so the app labels it “not validated”.
trust.lowBodyNoCount: Only {{pct}} of 2-hour windows in the test data contained a low. That is too few to train or check the chance of going low, so the app labels it “not validated”.
trust.lowAurocNote: AUROC for lows: 0.5 is chance level. Values near or below 0.5 mean these numbers must not be used as a hypo alarm.
trust.baselinesRmseNote: Forecast error (RMSE, mg/dL) at the chosen look-ahead. Lower is better; the best method in each column is in bold.
trust.baselinesAurocNote: AUROC for going above 180 in 2 hours. Higher is better; methods without a risk output show —.
trust.nbpDiffTitle: Change in past-curve error per patient (twin-recommended times minus …)
trust.nbpNull: Honest result: no clear benefit. Both 95% intervals cross zero, so letting the twin pick the prick times did not measurably beat fixed or random times in this data. The suggestion stays in the app as a convenience, not as a proven gain.
trust.nbpEffect: At least one interval does not cross zero; see the direction of the dots above.
trust.gap: Extra 1-hour error when the model is moved from one population to the other ({{setting}}).
trust.insulin: On ShanghaiT2DM, the 1-hour error is {{a}} mg/dL for insulin users and {{b}} mg/dL for others: the model does not represent insulin doses.
trust.gridNote: Number at the right: share in zones A+B (clinically acceptable). Reference: the hidden CGM.
trust.pending: This evaluation is still running. Its results will appear here when the report is written.
trust.englishOnly: These notes come straight from the evaluation reports, in English.

trust.recentCaption: Forecast error just after a finger-prick (within 90 minutes), against the same people and clock times when the twin had no reading after calibration.
trust.recentDiff: At 1 hour ahead, a recent prick changed the error by {{d}} mg/dL (95% interval {{lo}} to {{hi}}).
trust.recentHelps: The whole interval is below zero: a fresh reading clearly makes the forecast better.
trust.recentHurts: The whole interval is above zero: in this test a fresh reading did not make the forecast better.
trust.recentUnclear: The interval crosses zero, so this test cannot show a clear benefit.
trust.livingTitle: Living uncertainty: error and band by hours since the last reading
trust.livingCaption: With 2 pricks a day: forecast error, 90% band width and band coverage 1 hour ahead, grouped by hours since the last finger-prick. This checks whether the band the twin shows between readings stays honest.
trust.livingNote: Error and band width share one unit (mg/dL).
trust.recordingsNote: One dataset has more recordings than people: some people were recorded more than once.
trust.livingWidens: The band gets wider as the last reading gets older.
trust.livingFlat: Honest result: in this test the band did not get steadily wider as the last reading got older.
trust.livingCoverageOk: Coverage stayed within 5 points of the 90% target in every group.
trust.livingCoverageOff: In {{n}} group(s) coverage was more than 5 points away from the 90% target (red rows).
trust.widthNoteFull: Under each bar: average width of the 90% band in mg/dL. A wide band can cover well and still say little.

glossary.tir: Time in range: the share of time glucose stays between 70 and 180 mg/dL.
glossary.band: Shaded band: up to now it is the model's 5–95% spread (not calibrated); after now it is the 90% forecast band, calibrated up to 2 hours ahead. The calibrated range for now is shown on the Estimated card.
glossary.freshness: Freshness: how recently the twin saw a real reading. It fades as hours pass.
glossary.ladder: Sensor ladder: how many glucose readings the twin gets a day, from a full sensor down to none.
glossary.rmse: RMSE: the typical size of the forecast error, in mg/dL.
glossary.coverage: Coverage: how often the real value fell inside the band.
glossary.gmi: GMI: glucose management indicator, an estimate of HbA1c from glucose readings.
glossary.nbp: Next best prick (experimental): the time when a finger-prick is expected to teach the twin the most. In testing it did not beat fixed times.
glossary.projection: Projection: what could happen if habits stay the same. Not a prediction of your lab results.

explain.measured: A real reading: from a glucometer, a sensor or a lab report.
explain.estimated: The twin's best guess from your readings and its model of your body. It always comes with a range.
explain.simulated: What the model calculates would happen if you made a change. A simulation, not a proven effect.
explain.validated: Retrospectively evaluated: tested on held-out people from a named research dataset (not clinically validated). When the twin said “6 in 10”, we counted how often it really happened. See the Trust panel for the dataset and protocol.
explain.exploratory: Shown for curiosity. This part (for example, more than 2 hours ahead) was not tested, so treat it loosely.
explain.not_validated: Not checked: there was too little data to test this number. Do not rely on it.

about.title: About NemoTwins
about.body: NemoTwins is a multilingual glucose digital-twin research prototype. It shows what a model estimates, how uncertain that estimate is and where every number comes from. It is not a medical device and has not been clinically validated.
about.fishHint: A small decorative clownfish occasionally swims along the bottom of the page. It has no meaning and never appears during safety alerts, in reports or with reduced motion.
about.visionNote: Meal-photo recognition: {{model}} on Nebius Token Factory. It only suggests dish names for you to confirm; carbs come from the food table.
about.visionOff: Meal-photo recognition is switched off. Sample meals and entering dishes by hand still work.

references.title: Further reading from trusted health sources
references.note: General information from public-health and diabetes-society websites, found by web search (Tavily) on the topic only. Not about your twin, not personal medical advice.

calibratedNow.label: Calibrated 90% range now
calibratedNow.explain: Where your glucose most likely is at the replay time now. The model's spread is widened to the 90% range that held on people it had not seen (the 30-minute forecast calibration). This is the range to use.

particleSpread.label: Model spread (5–95%), not calibrated
particleSpread.explain: The 5th to 95th percentile of the twin's internal simulations at this time. It is not calibrated and is usually narrower than the calibrated 90% range, so it can look more certain than the twin really is.

forecastBand.label: 90% forecast band
forecastBand.explain: The forecast range at this future time, widened to match the calibrated 90% band measured at 30 to 120 minutes ahead. Beyond 2 hours it is exploratory.
